testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Using a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver if the driver is speaking.

questions.explanation: A hands-free phone is safer than a hand-held phone, but it can still distract you mentally. Talking on the phone takes your attention away from driving.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, start by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of air in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: On long trips, you should:
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving through the night or when you would normally be sleeping is dangerous.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Rely on your taillights to warn other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: A second conviction for operating a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher will result in:

options.text: Loss of your CDL for life.
Loss of your CDL for five years.
Loss of your CDL for one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of your CDL for life.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher. A first offense results in losing your CDL for one year. A second offense results in losing your CDL for life.

questions.question: Air pressure in a single air system should build up within:
questions.explanation: In a single air system, pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you must check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip, then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Driving distractions are physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with passengers), or both (using a hand-held phone).

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
Push the clutch out when the engine is close to idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is close to idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
questions.explanation: When stopping, brake smoothly and gradually. For a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on the whole time you are turning. Turn it off only when the turn is complete.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used for:

options.text: Making the air brakes work better.
Filling the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank lets you temporarily release spring brakes if they lock due to low air pressure. This gives you a short time to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert while driving?
questions.explanation: Drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. This is when tired driving crashes are most likely to happen.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal
The distance you travel from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance you travel from when you see a hazard until you decide to brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from when you decide to brake until you actually press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far you travel between deciding you must brake and actually hitting the brakes.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing and blinking a lot
Yawning a lot or rubbing your eyes

questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, forgetting what you just drove, missing exits, drifting from your lane, following too closely, and feeling restless. Staying in your lane is safe driving, not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should weight be placed?

options.text: As far to the left as possible

questions.explanation: Heavy cargo placed high up makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Put cargo as low as possible to keep the center of gravity low.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: Make sure they are connected to the battery
Make sure they are carrying fuel

questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what does fresh oil under your vehicle mean?
questions.explanation: Before your trip, check under the vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Finding any of these is a problem that needs attention.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you think you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. This helps you avoid aggressive driving behavior and keeps you and others safe.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Turn gently and do not pass other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil on the road. This creates a very slippery surface before the rain washes the oil away.

questions.question: The more alcohol in the body:

options.text: The quicker the liver will digest it.
The less effect it will have.
The longer it takes to remove from the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it takes to remove from the body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more alcohol you drink, the longer it takes your body to remove it.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third when driving on wet roads.

questions.question: If feeling drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Pull off the road safely and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road safely and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, stop and sleep. Driving while tired causes many fatal accidents.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle:

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you park. Use wheel chocks if needed.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will receive points if you:
questions.explanation: Each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line, the examiner counts it as an error.

questions.question: When doing a conventional parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it with your vehicle completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: Look for an escape ramp first. If none is available, find a flat area or uphill side road to stop your vehicle safely.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts means they may be loose.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, air pressure moves the slack adjusters through rods. This happens when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Tread of 3/32 of an inch in the grooves of the front tires

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: A commercial driver can use a cell phone while driving only if:

options.text: They use a hands-free cell phone, if allowed.
They are driving on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use a hands-free cell phone, if allowed.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving, use only a hands-free phone positioned close to you. Even hands-free phones can distract you. Know the cell phone laws in your state.

questions.question: To stop your vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move, you can:

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start to move, partly engage the clutch before you lift your foot from the brake pedal.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Be done the same way every time.
Not always include all items of concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you do not forget anything.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed.

questions.question: Your CDL will be revoked if:

options.text: You want to add an endorsement.
Your regular driver's license is revoked.
You have not paid a toll.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your regular driver's license is revoked.
questions.explanation: If your regular driver's license is revoked, canceled, or suspended due to traffic violations, you will lose your CDL. This does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps an engine work properly:

options.text: In both cold and hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: In both cold and hot weather.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze helps your engine in hot weather too.

questions.question: Reading a text message while driving is:

options.text: Allowed if you are not pulling a trailer.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door to see better.

questions.explanation: You should always check your mirrors. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before starting a trip:

options.text: They will get clean after driving a short distance.

questions.explanation: Before your trip, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt or anything blocking your view. Clean them if needed.

questions.question: A truck should be parked:

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: You cannot see everything behind you. Backing is always dangerous. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: Items on a flatbed:

options.text: Are usually heavy enough that they don't need to be tied down.
Should not be tied down if you drive slower than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers without sides, all cargo must be tied down to prevent it from moving or falling off.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while shifting gears:

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long, you may have trouble shifting into the next gear. Do not force the gear shift. Instead, return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up the engine to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be seen as:
questions.explanation: Drivers talking with passengers may not pay full attention to driving. Be careful when driving near distracted drivers.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: Shortly after changing a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Lower the tire pressure to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to recheck the lug nuts to make sure they are still tight.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, decide what to do quickly because:

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will move out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: When brakes fail on a downhill slope, act quickly. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle goes and the harder it becomes to stop.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and air brake systems from too much air pressure. It usually opens at 150 psi.
